subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs DeepServe vs CloudML
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@omniva.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@omniva.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:00:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs DeepServe vs CloudML

Hi Nina 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the test phase. Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow if you'd prefer to walk through this live.

Summary of what we heard (pain & goals):
- Primary pain: inconsistent response latency and high per-token cost on customer-facing triage flows (esp. peak hours).
- Goals: sub-200ms 95th percentile for single-string generation at 512 tokens, predictable cost < $0.02 per 1k tokens, and auditability for prompt / output provenance.
- Decision criteria: latency SLO, cost/unit, security controls (VPC/KMS), and quality regression on key prompt set (triage_open / triage_followup).

Competitive takeaways (from today's demo & logs you shared):
- DeepServe: strong throughput, but current integration lacked KV cache and costs spiked with burst traffic.
- CloudML: good managed offering but limited private deployment options and longer procurement lead time.
- Redwood (summary): built-in KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles for lower GPU cost, and Private/VPC options you asked about. See attached bakeoff spreadsheet with our head-to-head notes.

Open questions we captured:
1) Can you share 1-week request traces for the triage flows (anonymized) so we can size batch/caching configs?
2) Is audit log retention required for >12 months or is 90 days sufficient for now?
3) Do you have a security questionnaire we should return to your InfoSec?

Proposed next steps / tests we recommend:
- Redwood-run smoke test: we'll stand up a temporary private test deployment and run your sample prompt set for 3 days (we will provide scripts + metrics).
- Test metrics: 95p latency, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, qualitative quality diff vs current provider.
- Deliverables: bakeoff summary spreadsheet (attached), test plan (attached), and a 30-min results review + recommendation.

Attachments: 20261125-redwood-bakeoff-summary.xlsx, 20261125-test-plan.md

Action items:
- Nina/Rajesh: share anonymized trace (item 1) and preferred audit retention window (item 2) by next Tue (11/30).
- Marissa/Michael: provision test env and confirm timeline by EOD Thu (11/26).

Thanks  looking forward to running the tests.


Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198
https://www.redwoodinference.com

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@omniva.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@omniva.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs DeepServe vs CloudML

Thanks Marissa  great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide an anonymized 7-day trace by EOD Monday (11/29). Will remove PII and customer IDs.
- Audit retention: our legal team prefers 12+ months, but for the bakeoff 90 days is fine if longer retention impacts cost/architecture.
- Security questionnaire: attaching our standard vendor questionnaire (separate attachment - sending via procurement).

Couple of follow-ups: 
1) Can Redwood guarantee that the test environment will mimic our peak concurrency (we see spikes to ~350 concurrent reqs in triage)?
2) For quality regression, can you run an A/B test against current vendor with blinded eval so our product team can score without bias?

We'll aim to have procurement loop in next week once we see the test plan.

Thanks,
Nina
Head of Product Ops | OmniHealth
Nina.Patel@omniva.com | +1 617-555-0224

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@omniva.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@omniva.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs DeepServe vs CloudML

Hi Nina 

Short answers: yes and yes. A few specifics so expectations are clear:

- Concurrency: We'll provision a dedicated test pool and run a load profile that matches your ~350 concurrent baseline and a 500-concurrency spike for 15min windows. That will exercise batching and cache behavior.
- A/B quality: We'll run a blinded A/B on your prompt set and provide a scoring spreadsheet with randomized outputs so your product team can rate without knowing which vendor produced which response.
- Timeline: we'll provision the test env on Friday (11/27) and kick off the 3-day run Mon (11/30) once we receive the anonymized traces.

I've attached a short runbook and the test plan Marissa drafted. Laura will lead the operational side and be the day-of contact.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0147
